question: frac{(operatorname{cosec} θ-sin θ)(sec θ-cos θ)(tan θ+cot θ)}{cos θ(sec θ-tan θ)²(sec θ+tan θ)}=(1)/(1-{k)}, 0circ, then k = ?
solution:
**Formula used**

sin²a + cos² = 1

sec2a - tan2 = 1

Cosec2a - cot2 = 1

**Calculation**

frac{(operatorname{cosec} θ-sin θ)(sec θ-cos θ)(tan θ+cot θ)}{cos θ(sec θ-tan θ)²(sec θ+tan θ)}=(1)/(1-{k)}, 0circ

frac{(operatorname{cosec} θ-sin θ)(sec θ-cos θ)(tan θ+cot θ)}{cos θ(sec θ-tan θ)(sec² θ-tan² θ)}=(1)/(1-{k)}

frac{(operatorname{cosec} θ-sin θ)(sec θ-cos θ)(tan θ+cot θ)}{cos θ(sec θ-tan θ)}=(1)/(1-{k)}

frac{(operatorname{cosec} θ-sin θ)(sec θ-cos θ)(tan θ+cot θ)}{cos θsec θ-cos θtan θ)}=(1)/(1-{k)}

frac{(operatorname{cosec} θ-sin θ)(sec θ-cos θ)(tan θ+cot θ)}{1-sinθ}=(1)/(1-{k)}

⇒ [cos²θ/Sinθ × Sin²θ/cosθ × Sec2θ/tanθ]/[1 - sinθ]

⇒ 1/(1 - sinθ) = 1/(1 - k)

comparing both k = sinθ

**The answer is sinθ**
